finding_resolution.proof: Drop has exclusive mutable access after the final Arc owner disappears. OnceLock::take removes the owned FunctionEncoding; its byte length is saved, then explicit drop(encoding) destroys its Box<[u8]> before the shared ledger lock is acquired and retained is decremented. Subsequent automatic field destruction sees an empty OnceLock. Another product cannot spend this charge until the old encoded payload has been freed. A delay acquiring the ledger lock overcounts already freed bytes conservatively.
finding_resolution.concurrent_admission: retain_encoding still checks checked_add against min(first group capacity,current max_source_bytes) and allocates/installs/charges while holding the same group mutex. Published encoding is immutable, and the rechecked OnceLock admits at most one fragment per owner. The fix introduces no callback, recursive lock, owner cycle, or extra retained payload.
finding_resolution.checkpoint_lifecycle: FunctionSession clones/checkpoints and immutable entry owners retain the same group and charge until the final raw product owner. The encoding is removed/freed exactly once in final-owner Drop; independent groups and clear() retain the previously documented separate scope.
